newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble firm on client demand but o/n credits cheap.
newsitem.headline: Rouble firm on client demand but o/n credits cheap.

text.p: The rouble firmed on Monday as
bank clients sought funds for investing in government securities
but dealers said rouble credits remained cheap after the central
bank had lowered its rouble reserve requirements this month.
roubles/dollar May 19 midday May 19 early May 16 close

"Bank clients could be selling dollars either ahead of the T-bill auctions or to maintain current liquidity. T-bill investments are still attractive, given the low yields of (rouble) credits," National Reserve Bank chief dealer Dmitry Smirnov said.
On May 21 the Finance Ministry will auction four trillion roubles in 168-day GKO discount Treasury bills and seven trillion roubles in 364-day T-bills.
Dealers said rouble supply was higher after the central bank had lowered its requirements for rouble reserves of commercial banks by two percentage points from May 1.
But banks are not rushing to invest in dollars as the central bank's dollar/rouble bid/offer rates have been unchanged since last Tuesday, they added.

"Roubles are not leaving the market after the requirements become lower. Besides the central bank is not encouraging dollar buying as it is keeping its rates unchanged and this is another reason for the dollar's decline," a Mezhkombank dealer said.
